at_sea: The two-tense rule is captured, born, cast, and ruled in one sitting (commons ee7cc33; cairn unchanged at 1a8f941). The chain: Akien's observation (history creates noise — a model reader holds an outdated history bit as true) -> /idea 2026-08-15-akien-verbatim-2026-08-15-so-i (his prose verbatim, CC's response marked as translation) -> /intent (routed_forward; berth intent-20260815T121914-e07ff0be3cc0) -> /sorted cast as CONCEPT-PIECE (berth sorted-20260815T122335-7e1d8a67a946) -> ticket an-artifact-is-present-tense-or-past-tense-never-both filed with both berths -> ruling decisions/2026-08-15-an-artifact-is-present-tense-or-past-tense-never-both.json opened and confirmed. THE RULE: every artifact is exactly one tense — present-tense (charters, CLAUDE.md, MAP.md, state, code+comments) is REWRITTEN at each design shift, provenance as ticket-id pointers; past-tense (history, slates, voyages, decisions) is append-only per Law 7 and never loaded by default EXCEPT through a compiled current-truth face (charter state and the SessionStart slate injection are the legalizing precedents). Summarizing rides the PROVED crossing, never a periodic pass. Migrations default atomic; a slow one needs a cast ticket whose cursor solely owns the partway state. Casting forced one enabling act: concept-piece@v1's workflow table registered in node_classes/concept-piece.json (path THINKME->TICKETME->BUILDME->PROVEME->PROVED, TICKETME skippable, WATCHME free) — the version existing strings (ticket-and-task) already claimed.
